messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging @oncall-rotation for P1 — elevated latency across hosted inference (p95 spike). Affected region: us-west-2. Start: 2026-03-15T08:17:56Z. See /incidents/1772509876 for details.

carol: I'm on it, grabbing traces now. Can someone confirm customer-facing errors?

jia: Seeing spike in p95 from ~220ms -> ~1.9s across batch endpoints. p50 mostly unchanged. No 5xx surge in API gateway.

mike: Checking infra metrics: node-level CPU and steal are fine, but we have elevated kernel scheduling delays on a subset of worker hosts. DMARQ counters increased on nvme on two nodes.

sam: Customer impact: a handful of realtime customers reporting slow responses; most are degraded latency only, no payload errors. I've flagged high-traffic customers in case we need outreach.

carol: Good. Start live mitigation steps: 1) roll traffic off the suspect host pool to spare hosts, 2) enable fallback model variant (smaller quantized) for latency-critical routes. I'll coordinate with routing.

oncall-rotation-bot: @oncall-rotation assigned to @carol for the incident. Handoff ETA 5m.

lex: I pulled a flamegraph from traces around 08:18-08:30. The slow spans are dominated by kernel scheduling + a bunch of long syscalls: page faults and futex wait. Attaching snippet:

lex: ```
# top slow spans (sample)
span_id: 0x7a3c - inference.decode - duration: 1.6s
  events: kernel-futex-wait 0.8s, page-fault 0.4s, wait-io 0.3s
```

elaine: I saw an automated kernel update kubelet churn in us-west-2 earlier this morning. Can we correlate node list with schedule windows?

mike: Confirming: two kernel updates rolled out by autoupdater between 07:55-08:05 on hosts gw-uf-03 and gw-uf-07. They were supposed to be drained but drain failed due to a pod-eviction timeout, so workloads stayed and kernel moved under the hood.

jia: Hypothesis: kernel change altered scheduler behavior for our G168 driver path -> causing increased futex blocking under contended threads. That matches the futex-heavy traces.

carol: Timeline so far: 07:55 autoupdater started kernel rollouts. 08:05 drain timeout on two hosts. 08:17 alert fired for p95. 08:20 first mitigation: move routing away from gw-uf-03/07. 08:27 enabled fallback model on critical routes. 08:35 p95 trending down. We need to keep building timeline and attach logs.

sam: Pushed a patch to routing to exclude host metadata label 'kernel-rolling=true'. Changes applied at 08:20. Traffic dropped ~40% from suspect hosts by 08:23.

oncall-rotation-bot: Handoff: @carol is primary, @jia secondary.

lex: Sharing perf counters from gw-uf-03 before/after drain:

lex: ```
# gw-uf-03 perf snapshot 07:50
CPU cycles: normal
context-switches: 120/s
futex-waits: 30/s
page-faults: 2/s

# gw-uf-03 perf snapshot 08:10
context-switches: 420/s
futex-waits: 220/s
page-faults: 18/s
```

mike: That perf delta is big. fwdriver modules show increased kernel preemption. Also NVMe DMARQ errors spiking on those hosts, which may explain io wait contributing to page faults.

carol: For immediate RCA work: capture full dmesg, kernel versions, packages, and kube evict logs for gw-uf-03/07. Jia, can you take gw-uf-03? Mike take gw-uf-07. Lex, keep tracing correlation and perf counters. Elaine, coordinate with infra autoupdater team.

jia: On it. Pulling dmesg and /var/log/kubelet.log now.

mike: Collecting NVMe SMART logs and klogs. Also snapshotting running process list and container pids for inference runtime.

elaine: Infra confirms autoupdater rolled kernel 5.19.14 -> 5.19.20 with backported scheduler fixes. The rollout had an edge-case where drain --force did not evict pinned pods. We'll treat that as a rollout policy bug.

sam: Customer comms draft: "We're investigating increased latency impacting some requests in us-west-2 starting 08:17 UTC; mitigations are in place and latency is improving. We'll provide an RCA." Thoughts?

carol: Draft looks good. Add note that no request data was lost and fallbacks were applied. Set status page to partial degradation.

lex: Correlating trace IDs with host assignment: 63% of slow traces map to gw-uf-03/07, 27% to hosts that briefly queued requests while routing adjusted. The remainder looks normal.

jia: dmesg excerpt from gw-uf-03: ```
[08:02:11] kernel: nvme 4: error: queue command timeout
[08:02:14] kernel: CPU: 1 PID: 3421 blocked for more than 120 seconds
[08:05:00] kubelet: eviction failed: timeout waiting for pod kube-system/cool-pod
```

mike: gw-uf-07 SMART shows increased media errors beginning 08:00. Could be unrelated hardware flakiness exposed by kernel update. I'll mark both hosts as unhealthy.

carol: Decision log in-thread: 08:20 route off hosts (done), 08:27 enable quantized fallback (done), 08:33 mark hosts unhealthy and start live replacement (in progress).

lex: Perf counters after routing change (08:28): futex-waits on cluster aggregate dropped from 150/s to 35/s. p95 is down to ~320ms by 08:40. p50 steady at 200ms.

sam: Noting customer A reported issues until 08:30; sent update at 08:45. No escalations yet.

elaine: Autoupdater team: we'll suspend the remainder of the kernel rollout and investigate the drain failure hook. Also starting a post-deploy test to catch long futex waits.

carol: Next steps for RCA: - collect full host dumps + git versions of kernel config - reproduce locally if possible with same kernel + NVMe driver - run microbench futex stress to see scheduler behavior - correlate with pod eviction code path to understand why drain didn't evict pinned pods.

jia: Running a futex stress reproducer in a staging cluster with 5.19.20 now. Will post results.

mike: Hardware ops to replace NVMe (pending approval) for gw-uf-07. If hardware confirmed flaky, it's a multi-factor cause: kernel + failing storage -> long page faults -> futex backpressure.

carol: Good. I'm going to convert this incident to a coordination RCA channel and start drafting timeline + hypothesis section. Please paste any logs/traces into the RCA doc and tag entries with evidence links.

oncall-rotation-bot: Incident status updated: mitigated -> partial, now in post-mitigation RCA stage. Assigned: carol (lead), jia (traces), mike (hardware), lex (perf).

lex: Quick note to include in RCA: p95 spike shape was long tail (right-skewed), which matches blocking events rather than a sudden compute step regression. Kernel pages and NVMe IO latency lines up to blocking.

sam: I'll collect customer impact timeline per tenant and attach to RCA.

carol: Thanks team. If anyone finds evidence that rules out kernel change (e.g., identical behavior on non-updated hosts), call it out. Otherwise we'll track as 'likely root cause: kernel update interacting with degraded NVMe causing futex blocking and page faults -> latency regression'. We'll refine after reproducer and hardware checks. :thumbsup:

jia: Reproducer results: futex stress on 5.19.20 shows 2-3x increase in futex wake latency under thread contention compared to 5.19.14 on identical instance types. Attaching perf flame.

mike: NVMe replacement scheduled for gw-uf-07 at 11:00. gw-uf-03 is being reimaged.

elaine: Autoupdater will pause kernel rollout and add pre-drain pod pin check to avoid silent in-place kernel swaps.

carol: Closing notes: mitigations succeeded, customer impact limited, RCA lead to draft (links added). Will convert to follow-up bug tickets for autoupdater, kernel gating tests, and hardware triage. Great response, everyone.

incident-bot: Incident thread closed as 'RCA in progress' at 2026-03-15T09:02:00Z.
